lessons.name: automatica
lessons.summary: automatica is a Munich trade fair where robot manufacturers, automation suppliers, researchers, and users show how machines perform useful work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

automatica is a Munich trade fair where robot manufacturers, automation suppliers, researchers, and users show how machines perform useful work.

![Industrial robots demonstrated at automatica](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-automatica.webp)
*Industrial robots demonstrated at automatica. Source: [Official page](https://automatica-munich.com/en/trade-fair/exhibition-sectors/industrial-robotics/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Industrial robotics** means programmable machines doing production tasks; the fair covers handling, assembly, machine vision, and service robots.
- **The munich_i platform** connects AI and robotics through a summit, the AI.Society demonstrations, and Robothon, a collaborative software and hardware challenge.
- **The next advertised edition** runs June 22–25, 2027; the munich_i page explicitly labels its detailed content as the 2025 programme.

> **Key idea:** A working robot application needs the surrounding tools and integration, as well as the robot itself.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a software conference expo:** the arm is one library; cameras, grippers, and integration provide the dependencies that make an application work.
- **A useful comparison exercise:** choose two handling demonstrations and record the object, sensing method, and recovery when a grasp fails.
- **European Robotics Forum (ERF)** offers another route into the community; compare its workshop programme with automatica’s exhibition sectors.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2025 highlights** to recognize robot cells, the workspaces containing robots and their surrounding equipment.
2. **Browse industrial robotics and munich_i** before planning a visit; pick one technical question for each relevant exhibitor.
3. **Follow the official programme updates** and Robothon information; check the published entry conditions before proposing a student team.

lessons.name: Coupe de France de Robotique
lessons.summary: Coupe de France de Robotique brings teams together to build autonomous robots for a shared game and qualify for Eurobot.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Coupe de France de Robotique brings teams together to build autonomous robots for a shared game and qualify for Eurobot.

![Scene from the 2026 Coupe de France de Robotique](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-coupe-de-france-de-robotique.webp)
*Scene from the 2026 Coupe de France de Robotique. Source: [Official page](https://www.coupederobotique.fr), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Planète Sciences organizes the contest:** teams build physical robots, then meet around a game field with common rules.
- **The annual game** changes the engineering problem; the published 2027 theme is “The legend of Camelot,” with separate general and game rules.
- **Homologation** is the approval process before matches; the rules page separates robot requirements, gameplay, and field materials.

> **Key idea:** A competition rule becomes useful when you can turn it into a test of your robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Treat the rules like an API contract:** your robot can choose its implementation, but its size, actions, and scoring must satisfy the specification.
- **A first team exercise:** select one scoring action, list three failure cases, and demonstrate that action repeatedly before adding a second mechanism.
- **Eurobot** gives this French contest an international continuation; the shared game makes other teams’ design choices worth studying.

## How to engage

1. **Watch an archived match** and identify how the robots sense, move, and manipulate game objects; keep the edition’s rules beside you.
2. **Read the current general and game rules** together; note which approval documents are still marked as forthcoming.
3. **Use the public FAQ** for rule questions and the official registration information for the next edition; follow updates throughout the build.

lessons.name: Eurobot
lessons.summary: Eurobot is an international amateur robotics contest in which teams build robots for a common game and reach a shared final.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Eurobot is an international amateur robotics contest in which teams build robots for a common game and reach a shared final.

![Published photograph from the Eurobot contest](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-eurobot.webp)
*Published photograph from the Eurobot contest. Source: [Official page](https://www.eurobot.org), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **National organizing committees** run qualification routes; the association coordinates the international contest and encourages exchange between teams.
- **Common rules and a common field** make different mechanical and software designs comparable; the 2027 page publishes game rules and playground files.
- **Poolzor** is the registration platform; the participation guide specifies one account per structure, which can manage multiple teams.

> **Key idea:** The shared game gives your robot a test environment that other teams can reproduce.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a programming contest with hardware:** every team solves the same specification, but sensor errors and mechanical reliability also affect the result.
- **Coupe de France de Robotique** is the relevant French route; read the national and international instructions together before committing to participation.
- **A concrete reading exercise:** choose one game action, sketch its inputs and outputs, and compare how two teams execute it in archived finals.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2022 final** to understand the match format; use the current rules for any robot you plan to build.
2. **Read the participation guide** and identify your national organizing committee; qualification and registration are separate steps.
3. **Track Poolzor requirements and deadlines** from the official guide; avoid creating a test team, since its instructions say these cannot be deleted.

lessons.name: European Robotics Forum (ERF)
lessons.summary: European Robotics Forum is an annual meeting where robotics researchers, companies, users, and policy makers discuss technology and practical adoption.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

European Robotics Forum is an annual meeting where robotics researchers, companies, users, and policy makers discuss technology and practical adoption.

![Venue for European Robotics Forum 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-european-robotics-forum-erf.webp)
*Venue for European Robotics Forum 2026. Source: [Official page](https://eu-robotics.net/european-robotics-forum/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The euRobotics association and a local co-host** organize the forum; the programme connects research questions with problems faced by people using robots.
- **Workshops, exhibitions, and awards** create different ways to learn: listen to a focused discussion, inspect a system, or study a recognized application.
- **The event moves between cities:** the organizer’s current registration announcement points to Birmingham for ERF2027.

> **Key idea:** A useful visit starts with a robotics problem you can explain and a question someone there can answer.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Treat the programme like conference tracks:** choose sessions around one problem, such as perception or manipulation, instead of trying to cover every sector.
- **The euRobotics Awards** provide concrete examples of research reaching products; they help identify which claims deserve a closer technical reading.
- **A student preparation exercise:** choose two workshops and one exhibitor, then write a question about evaluation, deployment, or failure recovery for each.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the forum history video** to understand the mix of communities, then inspect a recent edition’s programme and exhibition.
2. **Use official registration and workshop announcements** when planning attendance; edition-specific schedules and conditions can change.
3. **Bring a concise project explanation:** describe the task, what already works, and the technical obstacle; use public event channels to continue the discussion.

lessons.name: euRobotics Awards
lessons.summary: euRobotics Awards recognize robotics research, entrepreneurship, technology transfer, and sustainability achievements through the European Robotics Forum.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

euRobotics Awards recognize robotics research, entrepreneurship, technology transfer, and sustainability achievements through the European Robotics Forum.

![euRobotics Awards ceremony at ERF2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-eurobotics-awards.webp)
*euRobotics Awards ceremony at ERF2026. Source: [Official page](https://eu-robotics.net/eurobotics-awards/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Different awards recognize different work:** the Georges Giralt PhD Award concerns doctoral research; the TechTransfer Award concerns research reaching industry.
- **Entrepreneurship and sustainability** also have recognition schemes; the 2026 ceremony additionally included Scientific Track best-paper awards.
- **A concrete 2026 winner:** TR4CE-Weld, “Tracing in Realtime 4 Cobot-Enhanced Welding,” took first place in the TechTransfer Award.

> **Key idea:** An award category tells you which kind of evidence a robotics project needs to demonstrate.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of separate review checklists:** a research contribution, a working business, and an industrial deployment answer different questions, even with similar robot hardware.
- **European Robotics Forum (ERF)** is where these communities meet; studying finalists can make its exhibition less overwhelming for a new student team.
- **A useful exercise:** compare two finalists and write one sentence each for the user problem, technical contribution, and evidence that the solution works.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2026 ceremony** and choose one project to investigate beyond its award title.
2. **Read the published winners and finalists** to find the exact project and institution names before looking for their technical work.
3. **Check each current call separately:** the 2027 Technology Transfer call describes research-to-industry collaboration; a student demo alone does not establish eligibility.

lessons.name: European Robotics Week (ERW)
lessons.summary: European Robotics Week connects local public events that help people experience robotics through demonstrations, workshops, and open labs.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

European Robotics Week connects local public events that help people experience robotics through demonstrations, workshops, and open labs.

![Published European Robotics Week event photograph](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-european-robotics-week-erw.webp)
*Published European Robotics Week event photograph. Source: [Official page](https://eu-robotics.net/european-robotics-week/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Locally organized activities** make up the week; universities, companies, schools, and community spaces show robotics to people with different backgrounds.
- **Hands-on outreach** means visitors can ask questions and try activities, rather than only watching polished clips of robots.
- **The 2026 preview in Bucharest** included education workshops and discussions about robotics in society; it illustrates the event’s broad public focus.

> **Key idea:** Explaining a robot to a visitor is a practical test of whether your team understands its behavior.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an open-source demo day:** the audience needs a clear entry point, visible behavior, and an explanation of what happens when something fails.
- **A possible 42AI activity:** show one robot task twice, changing one input, and ask visitors to predict the difference before running it.
- **European Robotics Forum (ERF)** addresses the professional community; ERW adds a public outreach route for sharing what students have built.

## How to engage

1. **Watch an earlier central-event video** to see the outreach setting, then find activities through the official events calendar.
2. **Choose a small demonstration** with a plain-language explanation of sensing, decisions, and movement; keep visitor interaction within the setup’s safe operating space.
3. **Use the event-submission channel** linked from the official ERW page if organizing an activity; consult the national coordinator information for local context.

lessons.name: European Robotics League (ERL)
lessons.summary: European Robotics League benchmarks robots through tasks in realistic environments, bringing research teams together to compare practical performance.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

European Robotics League benchmarks robots through tasks in realistic environments, bringing research teams together to compare practical performance.

![Robot activity at European Robotics League 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-european-robotics-league-erl.webp)
*Robot activity at European Robotics League 2026. Source: [Official page](https://eu-robotics.net/european-robotics-league/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Benchmarking** means testing systems under shared conditions so results can be compared, rather than relying on unrelated demonstration videos.
- **The league spans application settings:** its history includes consumer, professional, emergency, and smart-city robotics challenges.
- **ERL2026 took place in Scheveningen, The Hague,** on May 13–15; its published material includes indoor activities and outdoor beach conditions.

> **Key idea:** A robot that succeeds under one carefully arranged setup still needs testing under varied conditions.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of integration testing:** robot software, sensors, and movement must work together when the environment changes.
- **A replay exercise:** watch one ERL2026 sequence and record the task, environmental difficulty, human assistance, and observable outcome in four columns.
- **ELROB (European Land Robot Trial)** offers another view of field evaluation; compare its user-driven scenarios with the league’s published challenges.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the 2026 highlights** to see robots operating outside a clean laboratory demonstration.
2. **Read the event’s challenge descriptions** before choosing a development goal; reproduce one task locally and record failures as well as successes.
3. **Follow the official league announcements** for future participation requirements; use the photo and video archives to study prior setups and conditions.

lessons.name: HANNOVER MESSE and ROBOTICS AWARD
lessons.summary: HANNOVER MESSE is an industrial trade fair whose ROBOTICS AWARD recognizes market-ready robot applications in automation and logistics.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

HANNOVER MESSE is an industrial trade fair whose ROBOTICS AWARD recognizes market-ready robot applications in automation and logistics.

![GoodBytz receives the ROBOTICS AWARD 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-hannover-messe-and-robotics-award.webp)
*GoodBytz receives the ROBOTICS AWARD 2026. Source: [Official page](https://www.hannovermesse.de/en/press/press-releases/hannover-messe/robotics-award-2026-goes-to-goodbytz), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The award evaluates applications:** companies and institutions can submit robot-assisted solutions, including organizations that are not exhibiting at the fair.
- **Market-ready** means the call seeks products ready for practical use; a jury assesses innovation, industrial potential, and economic viability.
- **GoodBytz won in 2026** with an automated kitchen using compact Fanuc industrial robots to prepare individualized meals.

> **Key idea:** Industrial robotics is about delivering a complete service reliably, with the robot as one component.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of shipping a web service:** a clever algorithm matters, but customers also need dependable workflows and an application that solves their problem.
- **A useful case-study exercise:** split the GoodBytz kitchen into three responsibilities—handling ingredients, sequencing orders, and meeting food-processing requirements.
- **The automatica fair** provides another industrial-robotics exhibition to compare; inspect the actual application around an arm rather than judging its appearance.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the fair highlights** and identify complete production systems around the robots.
2. **Read the GoodBytz winner announcement** to connect the physical robot to its control software and intended users.
3. **Check the current award call** before planning a submission; use the published criteria to assess how far a student prototype is from deployment.

lessons.name: CYBATHLON
lessons.summary: CYBATHLON brings people with disabilities and engineering teams together to test assistive technologies on tasks from everyday life.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

CYBATHLON brings people with disabilities and engineering teams together to test assistive technologies on tasks from everyday life.

![Pilot Sammy Kunz trains with an assistance robot for CYBATHLON](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-cybathlon.webp)
*Pilot Sammy Kunz trains with an assistance robot for CYBATHLON. Source: [Official page](https://ethz.ch/en/news-and-events/eth-news/news/2024/10/team-rsl-at-cybathlon-when-four-legs-are-another-pair-of-hands.html), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The person using the technology is the pilot:** teams develop assistive systems around real activities such as climbing stairs or handling household objects.
- **The 2024 edition had eight disciplines,** including new races for vision assistance and assistance robots.
- **An assistance-robot example:** ETH’s Team RSL worked with pilot Sammy Kunz on a four-legged robot for activities such as brushing teeth and loading dishes.

> **Key idea:** The user’s ability to complete an everyday task matters more than an impressive isolated robot movement.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of usability testing for a physical interface:** the pilot’s feedback changes how the system is controlled, not merely its visual presentation.
- **ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab (RSL)** supplies a concrete case study linking robot movement, manipulation, and user needs.
- **A viewing exercise:** choose one assistance task and list the user command, robot action, and observable success condition before comparing approaches.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a 2024 race** and read the ETH coverage to understand the tasks and the role of the pilot.
2. **Study the Team RSL example** as a user-centered engineering process; distinguish what the pilot commands from what the robot executes.
3. **Check the official status page:** CYBATHLON is taking a strategic pause; use published materials for learning while awaiting any future event announcement.

lessons.name: ELROB (European Land Robot Trial)
lessons.summary: ELROB is a field trial where ground robots demonstrate practical capabilities in scenarios defined with their intended users.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ELROB is a field trial where ground robots demonstrate practical capabilities in scenarios defined with their intended users.

![Ground robot pictured on the ELROB official site](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-elrob-european-land-robot-trial.webp)
*Ground robot pictured on the ELROB official site. Source: [Official page](https://elrob.org), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A trial tests capability:** the organizer describes ELROB as a non-profit research activity, with demonstrations in realistic conditions.
- **The 2026 edition in Thun** covered convoy transport, outdoor mapping, shuttle transport, and search-and-rescue tasks.
- **A concrete scenario is CasEvac:** short for casualty evacuation, it asks a robot to find and drag a dummy body.

> **Key idea:** A field scenario reveals whether the complete system works beyond the assumptions of a lab setup.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of testing distributed software on real networks:** terrain, visibility, and communication conditions become part of the experiment.
- **A simple analysis exercise:** choose the shuttle scenario and separate its requirements into finding a route, moving safely, and reporting task completion.
- **EnRicH (European Robotics Hackathon)** applies a related trial format to hazardous environments; compare the scenario descriptions before choosing a student research direction.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2026 film** to recognize the outdoor platforms and testing environment.
2. **Read one scenario document** from the event page and list the robot inputs, expected actions, and conditions for observing success.
3. **Use official participation and visitor announcements** for future editions; begin with the published research material before proposing a field-trial entry.

lessons.name: Adopt AI hackathons (Artefact)
lessons.summary: Adopt AI hackathons are Artefact’s short team challenges for turning real-world AI problems into prototypes, linked to its Paris summit.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Adopt AI hackathons are Artefact’s short team challenges for turning real-world AI problems into prototypes, linked to its Paris summit.

![Grand Palais roof in the Adopt AI summit video preview](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-adopt-ai.webp)
*Grand Palais roof in the Adopt AI summit video preview. Source: [Official page](https://adoptai.artefact.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A hackathon** is a short build sprint: participants form teams, tackle a problem, and present a prototype rather than a finished product.
- **The programme spans several domains:** the 2026 listings include health, quantum computing, and a humanoid robot challenge; this is not a robotics-only competition.
- **A concrete example:** the health showcase describes 10 teams prototyping over three days, with mentors and challenges supplied by healthcare organizations.

> **Key idea:** A useful prototype starts with a real user’s problem, not with choosing an impressive AI model.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a compressed software release:** agree on one feature, build a testable version, and explain what works before the deadline.
- **Practice the software side first:** for a robotics proposal, separate image processing, robot control, and the user interface instead of promising an entire autonomous system.
- **Compare with Coupe de France de Robotique:** read both rule sets before deciding whether your team wants an AI prototype sprint or a robot competition.

## How to engage

1. **Watch Artefact’s past hackathon example** linked from the programme; it illustrates the organizer’s format, not a robot-building tutorial.
2. **Read an individual challenge page** for eligibility, location, team formation, and the required output; the health example required three days in person.
3. **Ask about hardware explicitly** before proposing a robotics demo; do not infer robot access from the summit’s broader AI branding.

lessons.name: AI for Good Global Summit and Robotics for Good Youth Challenge
lessons.summary: AI for Good connects ITU’s global AI summit with an educational robotics challenge where young teams build robots around real-world problems.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

AI for Good connects ITU’s global AI summit with an educational robotics challenge where young teams build robots around real-world problems.

![Young participants holding certificates at an AI for Good robotics activity](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-ai-for-good.webp)
*Young participants holding certificates at an AI for Good robotics activity. Source: [Official page](https://aiforgood.itu.int/robotics-for-good-youth-challenge/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **ITU**, the International Telecommunication Union, organizes AI for Good; its 2026 summit ran July 7–10 in Geneva.
- **The youth challenge** asks teams to design, build, and program a robot for a mission inspired by a global problem.
- **Platform-agnostic** means no mandatory robot kit: teams can choose their own hardware and source parts locally.
- **The 2025–2026 introduction** uses agriculture and food security as its theme; distinguish that season from the later health-emergencies edition.

> **Key idea:** A shared mission can compare robot solutions without requiring everyone to buy the same hardware.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a programming contest:** the mission is the specification, while the robot’s observable behavior is the test result.
- **A viewing exercise:** choose one task from the season introduction and write three columns: what the robot senses, what it decides, and what it moves.
- **Compare with Eurobot:** use the published missions to discuss task design, scoring, and what makes a demo understandable to spectators.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official challenge introduction** before reading the season-specific material; separate the general format from rules that change each year.
2. **Check age eligibility first:** this is a youth competition, not an automatic entry route for adult 42 students.
3. **Explore the public summit programme** for learning and demonstrations; use the challenge’s official channels to ask about educational collaboration rather than assuming team eligibility.

lessons.name: AMLD Intelligence Summit (Applied Machine Learning Days)
lessons.summary: AMLD Intelligence Summit is EPFL’s applied-AI gathering in Lausanne, where robotics demonstrations sit alongside talks, workshops, and broader discussions about intelligence.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

AMLD Intelligence Summit is EPFL’s applied-AI gathering in Lausanne, where robotics demonstrations sit alongside talks, workshops, and broader discussions about intelligence.

![Audience applauding at Applied Machine Learning Days](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-amld.webp)
*Audience applauding at Applied Machine Learning Days. Source: [Official page](https://www.appliedmldays.org/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **EPFL’s AI Center** organizes the summit; it grew from Applied Machine Learning Days into a wider discussion of artificial and human intelligence.
- **The 2026 edition** ran February 10–12 at Lausanne’s SwissTech Convention Center, with 24 tracks and 18 workshops across AI topics.
- **The robotics opening announcement** listed GOAT, a construction robot, a crawling robotic hand, and ANYmal tackling obstacles, with EPFL and ETH professors explaining the science.

> **Key idea:** Seeing several robot bodies solve different tasks helps separate a general AI technique from a particular machine’s capabilities.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a developer conference:** a keynote gives the architecture overview; workshops and demonstrations expose the implementation questions you should investigate next.
- **A concrete comparison:** take the announced construction robot and ANYmal; write one success condition for building and another for crossing an obstacle.
- **ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab (RSL)** is a related map stop for exploring Marco Hutter’s legged-robot research after the summit overview.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2026 day-one recap** to picture the event, then read the robotics announcement for the named demonstrations.
2. **Browse the 2026 archive** and choose one speaker or topic; prepare a specific question about how an experiment was tested.
3. **Use the official AMLD site** for future programmes and participation details; do not assume every track or workshop is about robotics.

lessons.name: Automate (US trade show)
lessons.summary: Automate is a US trade show where robotics and automation suppliers demonstrate the equipment and software used to make industrial tasks work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Automate is a US trade show where robotics and automation suppliers demonstrate the equipment and software used to make industrial tasks work.

![Students and educators visiting the Automate exhibition](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-automate.webp)
*Students and educators visiting the Automate exhibition. Source: [Official page](https://www.automateshow.com/attend/students-and-educators), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Automation** means using machines and software to carry out work; Automate brings robotics, vision, motion control, and related software onto one exhibition floor.
- **A3**, the Association for Advancing Automation, produces the event; its 2026 recap describes four days at Chicago’s McCormick Place.
- **Live demonstrations** sit alongside keynotes and conference sessions; the recap discusses simulation, robot programming, and learning skills from demonstrations.

> **Key idea:** An industrial robot becomes useful when sensing, software, and the surrounding production process work together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a dependency graph:** a robot arm is one package; cameras, gripping tools, and control software are dependencies needed for the complete application.
- **A practical viewing exercise:** pick two demonstrations from the recap and record the object handled, the sensing method, and what counts as a completed task.
- **Compare with automatica:** use the US and Munich exhibitions to investigate similar industrial problems without treating either show as a beginner robot-building course.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2026 highlights** and use the written recap to distinguish working applications from broader predictions about future robots.
2. **Choose one technical question** before exploring exhibitors: for example, how does a demonstration recover when an object is misplaced?
3. **Check the official visitor pages** before planning travel; the homepage now advertises May 10–13, 2027 in Las Vegas, not the 2026 Chicago venue.

lessons.name: BaselHack
lessons.summary: BaselHack is a regional hackathon where developers, designers, and other participants build prototypes together; it is not a dedicated robotics competition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

BaselHack is a regional hackathon where developers, designers, and other participants build prototypes together; it is not a dedicated robotics competition.

![BaselHack participants working together around laptops](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-baselhack.webp)
*BaselHack participants working together around laptops. Source: [Official page](https://www.baselhack.ch/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The format is a build weekend:** the 2025 archive describes teams producing prototypes within 48 hours across AI, data, sustainability, and inclusion.
- **GuideMe is a concrete industrial example:** Endress+Hauser’s 2024 challenge asked teams to generate assembly instructions from a sequence of images.
- **The link is software for physical work:** GuideMe concerns assembly documentation, not controlling a robot; robot hardware availability is unknown from these pages.

> **Key idea:** An industrial challenge can teach useful robotics-adjacent software skills without involving a moving robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a group programming sprint:** agree on input and output formats early so teammates can build separate pieces that join into one demo.
- **Try the GuideMe pattern:** use three photos of a harmless assembly task as input and produce three ordered instructions; check whether their order matches the photos.
- **Compare with Adopt AI hackathons (Artefact):** both offer prototype-building contexts; inspect individual briefs rather than assuming that either provides a robotics track.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2022 aftermovie** on the organizer’s public LinkedIn post to see participants and hear about the event’s collaborative format.
2. **Read the archive and GuideMe brief** before proposing a team; separate a demonstrated past challenge from an announced future opportunity.
3. **Use the website’s community channels** to ask about upcoming challenges and hardware suitability; prepare a software-only fallback rather than assuming equipment is supplied.

lessons.name: CeTI Mobile Robotics Hackathon
lessons.summary: CeTI Mobile Robotics Hackathon brings participants together at TU Dresden to build and test mobile-robot prototypes with supplied hardware and mentors.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

CeTI Mobile Robotics Hackathon brings participants together at TU Dresden to build and test mobile-robot prototypes with supplied hardware and mentors.

![Mobile Robotics Hackathon participants testing a rover beside a laptop](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-ceti.webp)
*Mobile Robotics Hackathon participants testing a rover beside a laptop. Source: [Official page](https://mobile-robotics.eu/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two days of building:** the [2026 recap](https://mobile-robotics.eu/) documents 103 participants and six challenge tracks at TU Dresden’s Barkhausenbau on October 10–11.
- **Mobile robots** move through their surroundings; the event provided drones, legged robots, rovers, and service robots rather than just software problems.
- **Hardware and guidance:** [CeTI’s report](https://ceti.one/mobile-robotics-hackathon-2026/) lists Spot, TurtleBots, HoloLens interfaces, and mentors available around the clock.
- **Teams worked across disciplines:** participants rewired components and extended existing hardware with software.

> **Key idea:** A robot demo depends on software, hardware, and testing working together, not on code alone.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an integration sprint:** separate the robot interface, task logic, and demonstration so teammates can work independently before connecting their pieces.
- **Try a viewing exercise:** pause the recap at three robot scenes; list what each robot senses, decides, and moves. Mark anything the video cannot establish.
- **Compare with BaselHack:** decide whether your team wants a general prototype sprint or an event explicitly offering mobile-robot hardware.

## How to engage

1. **Watch CeTI’s official recap** to picture the workspace, machines, and team activity before choosing a project idea.
2. **Use the event site’s public contact route** to ask about a future edition, beginner support, and equipment; the site says another edition is being planned.
3. **Prepare one small behavior** you could demonstrate and test repeatedly; confirm future hardware access.

lessons.name: Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL 2026)
lessons.summary: CoRL 2026 is the Austin edition of an international research conference on the intersection of robotics and machine learning.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

CoRL 2026 is the Austin edition of an international research conference on the intersection of robotics and machine learning.

![Official CoRL Austin logo with cowboy hat and city skyline](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-corl.webp)
*Official CoRL Austin logo with cowboy hat and city skyline. Source: [Official page](https://www.corl.org/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Robot learning** brings machine learning into robotics; [CoRL’s introduction](https://www.corl.org/) identifies this intersection as the conference’s focus.
- **The 2026 edition** runs November 9–12 in Austin, Texas: three main-conference days followed by workshops, according to the official programme.
- **Physical demonstrations matter:** the [demo call](https://www.corl.org/contributions/call-for-demos) requires at least one physical robot, not simulation alone.
- **Research tools count too:** the call welcomes systems for collecting data, remote robot operation, education, and new hardware, alongside learning methods running on robots.

> **Key idea:** A convincing robot-learning result connects a method to observable behavior on a real machine.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a research code review:** ask what changed, what evidence supports it, and whether somebody else could reproduce the result.
- **Try a three-column note:** while watching one presentation, record its input, robot action, and evaluation. Write “unknown” wherever the evidence is missing.
- **Compare with EnRicH (European Robotics Hackathon):** consider how research methods could face practical field tasks.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official Day 1 recording** and choose one presentation to study.
2. **Use the programme** to find sessions, then follow the conference’s contribution pages to understand the evidence expected from researchers.
3. **Treat the demo call as a benchmark:** plan a small physical demonstration first; the published 2026 submission deadline is past, not a standing invitation.

lessons.name: EnRicH (European Robotics Hackathon)
lessons.summary: EnRicH is a research-oriented robotics trial where teams test machines for hazardous-environment tasks at Austria’s never-operated Zwentendorf nuclear power plant.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

EnRicH is a research-oriented robotics trial where teams test machines for hazardous-environment tasks at Austria’s never-operated Zwentendorf nuclear power plant.

![Tracked EnRicH robot reaching toward a valve inside Zwentendorf](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-enrich.webp)
*Tracked EnRicH robot reaching toward a valve inside Zwentendorf. Source: [Official page](https://www.fkie.fraunhofer.de/en/departments/cms/EnRicH.html), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A trial, not a winner hunt:** the [organizer](https://enrich.european-robotics.eu/) describes EnRicH as non-profit research and development, testing robots in realistic scenarios.
- **The setting is concrete:** [Fraunhofer FKIE](https://www.fkie.fraunhofer.de/en/departments/cms/EnRicH.html) identifies the never-operated Zwentendorf nuclear plant as the venue.
- **The 2025 tasks** included building maps, measuring radiation, closing valves, and finding rescue dummies; the [rules](https://enrich.european-robotics.eu/enrich-2025/) made radiation measurement mandatory.
- **Communication is difficult:** concrete walls and metal interiors challenge radio links; participants cannot walk alongside robots during runs.

> **Key idea:** Useful field robotics means completing a task despite awkward terrain, limited visibility, and unreliable communication.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of integration testing outside your laptop:** a navigation component must work with sensors, communications, and movement in the same deployment.
- **Try a software-only exercise:** invent three readings with positions and values, then render them on a map; label them synthetic, not real radiation measurements.
- **Compare with CeTI Mobile Robotics Hackathon:** compare its hardware access with EnRicH’s specialist equipment requirements.

## How to engage

1. **Watch EuropeanRobotics’ 2025 film** to see the environment and machines.
2. **Read the scenario and participation rules** before proposing a team; use the organizer’s public channels to ask about readiness and future participation.
3. **Keep beginner experiments simulated:** the real trial uses radiation sources under official controls; do not reproduce those conditions independently.

lessons.name: ESA-ESRIC Space Resources Challenge
lessons.summary: The ESA-ESRIC Space Resources Challenge tests technologies for finding, collecting, processing, and using local materials to support future lunar exploration.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The ESA-ESRIC Space Resources Challenge tests technologies for finding, collecting, processing, and using local materials to support future lunar exploration.

![FZI robotic equipment photographed during the second Space Resources Challenge](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-esa-esric.webp)
*FZI robotic equipment photographed during the second Space Resources Challenge. Source: [Official page](https://src.esa.int/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The organizers** are the European Space Agency and European Space Resources Innovation Centre; their [challenge site](https://src.esa.int/) describes a programme launched in 2021.
- **Prospecting means finding resources:** the [first challenge](https://src.esa.int/the-challenge-2021-2022/) tested robotic prototypes on terrain representing the Moon, on Earth.
- **The second challenge** asked robots to collect and size-sort simulated lunar surface material at LUNA, a terrestrial lunar-test facility.
- **Regolith** means loose surface material; [the second-edition brief](https://src.esa.int/space_resources_challenge_2025/) distinguishes collecting it from preparing useful feedstock. The third edition turns toward construction with local resources.

> **Key idea:** Space-resource robotics is a chain of practical tasks, not simply driving a rover across a lunar-looking landscape.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a data-processing pipeline:** acquiring raw input and producing usable output are different stages, each needing its own measurable result.
- **Try a planning exercise:** draw three boxes—collect, transport, sort—and write one success measurement for each. Treat this as a proposed exercise, not official scoring.
- **Compare with EnRicH (European Robotics Hackathon):** compare environmental constraints before selecting a robot design.

## How to engage

1. **Watch ESRIC’s second-edition field film** to see robots in a ground-based test.
2. **Read the second-edition brief and questions** to understand the task; its described teleoperation means remote human control, not necessarily autonomous decision-making.
3. **Check the current challenge page** for public application channels; past missions and eligibility are not permanent rules.

lessons.summary: Chaos Communication Congress is an annual CCC gathering for talks, workshops, and hands-on technology projects; 40C3 is its 2026 edition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Chaos Communication Congress is an annual CCC gathering for talks, workshops, and hands-on technology projects; 40C3 is its 2026 edition.

![Speaker and live craft demonstration in the official 39C3 opening recording](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-congress.webp)
*The opening of 39C3 (2025), not 40C3; pajowu and Stella / media.ccc.de. Source: [Official page](https://media.ccc.de/v/39c3-opening-ceremony), CC BY 4.0.*

## What they do in robotics

- **The series, not a robot contest:** the [official introduction](https://events.ccc.de/congress/2026/infos/) describes a four-day event organized by the Chaos Computer Club and volunteers.
- **Assemblies** are shared spaces for collaborative projects and hands-on hacking, described in the [40C3 assembly announcement](https://events.ccc.de/en/2026/10/18/40c3-assemblies/).
- **A robotics entry point:** use those project spaces to discuss sensors, electronics, or a small robot prototype; this is a suggested approach, not a promised robotics programme.
- **The recording is from 39C3 (2025):** media.ccc.de's official opening introduces that edition. It is not a preview of the 40C3 programme.

> **Key idea:** Congress is useful as a place to exchange practical knowledge, not as a ready-made robotics curriculum.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an open-source meetup:** a working prototype and a precise question can start a better conversation than a polished pitch.
- **Try a tiny demo:** prepare a sensor reading, its timestamp, and a plot. Ask how someone would diagnose missing measurements.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 39C3 opening** for a concrete view of a previous Congress, clearly separated from current-edition information.
2. **Read the 40C3 newcomer FAQ** before planning equipment or activities; it restricts flying objects and asks participants to respect photographic consent.
3. **Follow current assembly guidance** before proposing a shared project space; do not treat previous-edition arrangements as permanent rules.

lessons.name: European Rover Challenge
lessons.summary: European Rover Challenge is an international space-robotics competition where teams test rover skills on a Mars-like outdoor course.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

European Rover Challenge is an international space-robotics competition where teams test rover skills on a Mars-like outdoor course.

![Wheeled rover crossing the European Rover Challenge Marsyard in front of spectators](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-erc.webp)
*A rover on the European Rover Challenge Marsyard. Source: [Official page](https://roverchallenge.eu/robotics-competition/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Rovers** are mobile robots built to explore terrain. The [competition overview](https://roverchallenge.eu/robotics-competition/) describes tasks on the Marsyard, a ground-based test area.
- **Navigation** means choosing and following a route; the event's navigation task includes reaching checkpoints on the course.
- **Manipulation** means moving objects with a robot mechanism. The maintenance task asks a rover to operate panel components, including switches and a connector.
- **Probing** tests finding and retrieving objects. The presentation task also asks teams to explain their engineering decisions to judges.

> **Key idea:** A convincing rover must combine movement, object handling, and an explanation of why its design works.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of an integration test:** perception, navigation, and arm control must cooperate on the same physical system rather than pass isolated software tests.
- **Start smaller than a Mars rover:** propose a tabletop exercise where a camera detects a marker and a simulated robot visits its position.
- **Measure one result:** record how many target positions your exercise reaches correctly before adding more complex behaviour.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2022 summary** to see the course, robots, and team activity; it documents an earlier edition.
2. **Read the task overview** and pick navigation or maintenance as a learning target, not the entire rover at once.
3. **Use the Competitor Zone** to inspect participation guidance. It describes interdisciplinary teams, including software roles; confirm current eligibility before planning an entry.

lessons.name: Eurosatory
lessons.summary: Eurosatory is a land and airland defence-and-security exhibition where demonstrations include unmanned ground vehicles and drones.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Eurosatory is a land and airland defence-and-security exhibition where demonstrations include unmanned ground vehicles and drones.

![Panel and audience discussing AI and automation at Eurosatory 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-eurosatory.webp)
*An AI-and-automation conference session at Eurosatory 2026. Source: [Official page](https://eurosatorymedia.tv/en/photos), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **An industry exhibition:** the [organizer's media service](https://eurosatorymedia.tv/en/a-propos) identifies COGES as organizer and Paris Nord Villepinte as the 2026 venue.
- **UGV means unmanned ground vehicle:** the [official demonstration index](https://eurosatorymedia.tv/en/infos-contenus) lists Rider UGV and Rheinmetall Mission Master platforms.
- **Drones** are also shown in those demonstrations. A vehicle without an onboard driver is not automatically making every decision autonomously.
- **Interviews and demonstrations** provide different evidence: [Eurosatory News](https://eurosatory.news/) offers event replays, while the media index identifies specific systems in demonstration footage.

> **Key idea:** Use a defence exhibition to examine system constraints and evidence, not to equate an impressive demonstration with proven autonomy.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a software demo versus a test report:** seeing a feature run once does not reveal failure rates or how much human control it required.
- **Make uncertainty explicit:** label autonomy level, communication range, and reliability as unknown unless a specific source documents them.
- **Keep the exercise civilian:** translate observations into inspection or remote-assistance questions, rather than designing weapon functions.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the 2026 best-of film** published by the media-service producer and linked through the official media ecosystem.
2. **Use the demonstration index** to locate named robotic platforms rather than treating all exhibition vehicles as robots.
3. **Compare an interview with footage:** write one documented capability and one unanswered question. Recheck visitor conditions through current public event channels before attending.

lessons.name: Field Robot Event
lessons.summary: Field Robot Event is a student competition where autonomous agricultural robots must work in real outdoor fields rather than only in a laboratory.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Field Robot Event is a student competition where autonomous agricultural robots must work in real outdoor fields rather than only in a laboratory.

![Field Robot Event robot navigating maize rows](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-field-robot.webp)
*A field robot navigating between crop rows at Field Robot Event. Source: [Official page](https://www.fieldrobotevent.eu/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Agricultural robotics** applies sensing and motion to farming tasks. The [official history](https://www.fieldrobotevent.eu/about) describes an event founded in 2003 at Wageningen University.
- **Outdoor autonomy** means operating without continuous human steering under field conditions. The event emphasizes student-developed robots beyond the laboratory.
- **Rows are navigation constraints:** the [2025 participant report](https://robotika.cz/competitions/fieldrobot/2025/en) documents maize-row navigation, fruit mapping, and other tasks.
- **Freestyle** gives teams room for a chosen demonstration. That report also shows development work, recordings, and results, not just finished promotional footage.

> **Key idea:** Field conditions turn apparently simple navigation into a test of reliable perception and movement.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of testing outside localhost:** software that works on saved images may behave differently when lighting, plants, and robot motion change together.
- **Try a low-cost exercise:** take your own crop-row photographs and draw the estimated free path between plants; this is a proposed learning exercise, not an official task.
- **Check failures first:** compare your estimate on clear and partially hidden rows before connecting any steering commands to hardware.

## How to engage

1. **Watch CULS Robotics' 2025 task recording:** it is a participant's run, uploaded by robotikacz, not an organizer-wide overview.
2. **Read the official history** to understand the competition's educational purpose and interdisciplinary roots.
3. **Follow the official event site** for the current host and instructions. Past reports do not replace current rules.

lessons.name: Formula Student Germany - Driverless Cup
lessons.summary: Formula Student Germany’s Driverless Cup challenges university teams to build self-driving racing cars and demonstrate both driving performance and engineering understanding.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Formula Student Germany’s Driverless Cup challenges university teams to build self-driving racing cars and demonstrate both driving performance and engineering understanding.

![Driverless Formula Student car on track](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-fsg-driverless.webp)
*Trackdrive at Formula Student Germany. © FSG - Felix Lodholz. Source: [Official page](https://www.formulastudent.de/fsg/about), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **A car becomes a robot** when sensing, decisions, and motion work together without an onboard driver. FSG's [official overview](https://www.formulastudent.de/fsg/about) explains its self-driving competition.
- **Driverless Cup disciplines** include acceleration, skidpad, autocross, trackdrive, and engineering design. Skidpad is a cone-marked figure-eight driving test.
- **Trackdrive** tests repeated autonomous driving on a course; engineering design asks teams to explain how and why their system works.
- **Results are public:** the [2026 results page](https://www.formulastudent.de/fsg/results/2026) separates Driverless Cup overall and discipline results, so readers can compare different aspects of performance.

> **Key idea:** Autonomous racing rewards an integrated, explainable engineering system, not just a fast perception model.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of a real-time service:** a correct answer arriving too late can still be unusable when the vehicle is moving.
- **Start in simulation:** propose detecting cone positions in saved images, then producing a path between them; do not begin with a moving full-size car.
- **Learn from the design requirement:** document one failure case and your reason for choosing a solution, rather than reporting only a successful lap.

## How to engage

1. **Watch FSG's driverless-participation academy recording** for an engineering perspective; its 2018 advice is historical, not the current rulebook.
2. **Read the official competition overview** to distinguish the Driverless Cup from the wider Formula Student Germany event.
3. **Open current Rules & Documents** before considering an entry. Use the current driverless specification and safety requirements.

lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Global Industrie is a French industrial exhibition where visitors can see robotics, automation, and production technologies alongside the companies that integrate them.

![Presentation at Global Industrie](/img/lessons/orgs_event_1-global-industrie.webp)
*A presentation in Global Industrie’s innovation area. Source: [Official page](https://www.global-industrie.com/univers/robotique), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Industrial tasks** give robots a purpose: the [robotics sector page](https://www.global-industrie.com/univers/robotique) lists welding, painting, assembly, handling, and service applications.
- **Mobile robots** include AGVs, automatically guided vehicles, and AMRs, autonomous mobile robots. Both appear in the event's robotics offering.
- **Integrators** combine robots, tooling, and other equipment into a working installation; the official sector page identifies them as partners in robotization projects.
- **Beyond individual machines:** the [event presentation](https://www.global-industrie.com/presentation) describes demonstrations and reconstructed production lines. GI TV adds interviews and discussions with industrial participants.

> **Key idea:** An industrial robot is one component of a production workflow; the useful question is what process it improves.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Think of API integration:** a clever module helps only when its inputs, outputs, and failure handling match the surrounding system.
- **Pick one workflow:** for example, propose moving a box from storage to a workstation. Draw where sensing, transport, and human decisions enter.
- **Ask a measurable question:** define success and what happens if the destination is blocked.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the official 2026 connected-warehouse video** to see how logistics equipment fits together rather than studying a robot in isolation.
2. **Explore the robotics sector page** and choose one application and one integrator to investigate using their public material.
3. **Use GI TV and current visitor information** to prepare a focused visit: bring three questions about task, operating conditions, and evidence of reliability.
